correctness.rationale: For 2 beta(n)=n multiplicative beta(p^a)=(p^{a+1}+(-1)^a)/(p+1), n must be even. Under omega<=2 either n=2^a (only a=1) or 2^a p^b. The exact ratio beta(p^b)/p^b=3/(4+(-1)^a 2^{1-a})<=4/5 for a>=2 and >=(p-1)/p excludes p>=7. p=5 forces a=3,b=1, n=40. For p=3 even b the left valuation forces a=1 (excluded); odd b requires even a and yields 3^{b+1}=2^{a+1}+1, hence (3^{(b+1)/2}-1)(3^{(b+1)/2}+1)=2^{a+1}, forcing factors 2 and 4: a=2,b=1, n=12. n=2 also works, and n=252 shows omega=3 possible. Independent exact enumeration n<=100000 confirmed all support<=2 hits.
residual_risks: The older literature tabulates witnesses and may contain an overlooked unindexed elementary classification of the two-prime case.
The necessary range bound uses this multiplicative alternating divisor-sum beta, not the ordinary sum-of-prime-divisors beta of record two.
Independent finite checks up to 100000 do not prove the classification beyond the symbolic ratio/parity argument.
